Darlington, N. D., Nov. 10.—Death which Thursday stalked bus carrying Minot State Teachers College gridders to Valley City remained on guard here and at Harvey, N. D., Saturday as doctors labored to save the lives of two youths.

Ora Marean of Minot, assistant football coach, and Allan Auffurth, Minot, co-captain, were killed Thursday night when the bus in which they were going to the game scheduled with Valley City State Teachers college turned over on a corner near Heaton, N. D., a short distance from here.

Of the seven persons in the two hospitals, physicians reported, two are in critical condition.

Charles Scott of Minot, believed in the most serious condition of the seven, has a dangerous head wound and internal injuries. He is in hospital here.

At Harvey, two of the youths hospitalized are believed out of danger. The third, Ted Brown, Minot, is suffering from concussion of the brain and has serious cuts on his head. He regained partial consciousness Friday.

Hospital attendants reported those least seriously injured will be ready to leave for Minot within a day or two.

Dean Stevens, Minot, is in the Harvey hospital with a dislocated shoulder and Arthur Heath is in the same hospital with severe bruises.
